newsitem.title: USA: Illinois judge won't suppress tobacco papers.
newsitem.headline: Illinois judge won't suppress tobacco papers.

text.p: Illinois Cook County Circuit Court Judge Richard Neville on Monday denied a request from tobacco industry lawyers to prevent release of sensitive internal documents by Liggett Group, said David Kistenbroker, attorney for the Illinois Attorney General's office.
"This is a distinct victory for the people of Illinois, who have a right to prosecute their case against tobacco," Kistenbroker told Reuters at the courthouse.

Neville ordered Liggett to deliver to him by Friday, under seal, certain documents the cigarette maker agreed last week to release in an historic settlement between it and 22 U.S. Attorneys General, Kistenbroker said.
He said Neville will review the documents, then decide within 30 days what to do with them.
Liggett asserted in court that it would comply with the judge's order, Kistenbroker said.

Tobacco industry lawyers had asked Neville to keep the documents under wraps until a North Carolina court rules on a related preliminary injunction request in that state, where the industry has won a temporary restraining order against release of the Liggett documents.

"We came in and asked for our own counter-injunction, saying to the judge that he didn't have to pay a hoot of attention to the North Carolina judge. We asked him to affirmatively order Liggett to bring those documents here to this courtroom and he has so ordered," Kistenbroker said.

Liggett broke ranks with other tobacco companies last week by agreeing to settle with the 22 attorneys general, who are suing the companies to recoup Medicaid health costs of poor smokers. Liggett is owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd.

In the settlement agreement, Liggett admitted that smoking is addictive and said it would turn over certain documents that could shed light on how much Liggett and other tobacco company executives knew about smoking's health risks and whether they purposely marketed cigarettes to young people.
